invention.ref: Coffeehouses and small long-handled pots appeared in Ottoman Istanbul in the mid-16th century
invention.ref_zh: 十六世纪中叶奥斯曼伊斯坦布尔出现咖啡馆与长柄小壶

popularization.ref: Distinctive lidless cezve form associated with foam-rich Turkish coffee becomes common
popularization.ref_zh: 无盖cezve形制与带沫土耳其咖啡做法在十八世纪更常见

sources.title: Turkish Coffee Culture — Turkish Ministry of Culture (TEDA)

notes: 咖啡进入奥斯曼约在十六世纪中叶，但今日所见无盖cezve定型可能更晚；精确发明年来源偏弱，主年份取伊斯坦布尔咖啡馆兴起年代。
notes_en: Coffee reached the Ottomans in the mid-16th century, but today’s lidless cezve may have solidified later; exact invention dating is thin, so the primary mark follows Istanbul coffeehouse emergence.
summary_zh: cezve是煮土耳其咖啡的长柄小壶；约十六世纪中叶随伊斯坦布尔咖啡馆兴起，后世成为无盖铜壶的典型形制。
summary_en: The cezve is the long-handled pot for Turkish coffee. It appeared alongside mid-sixteenth-century Istanbul coffeehouses and later settled into the familiar lidless copper form.
